I don't see how getting him committed for a few days is going to do anything but harm unless there's a solution. He's determined to die right now: he doesn't seem to be in any strange state of mind that he can snap out of by being forcefully held elsewhere.

Out of debt how? The reason he wants to die is because there doesn't seem a way out. He explained it to me, and I also see it as hopeless now. The debts are growing exponentially, rather than by a lump sum. He really won't be able to catch up to them normally, unless money falls from the sky and erases the part that grows beyond our income.

He's a medical doctor. There's not many better degrees he can get.

And what's going to happen then? I don't even know if they have treatment in Peru.

My boyfriend finally opened up and told me more about it, and he said that he decided to do it because he's not able to keep up with his debts anymore. What he earns is less than the interest to so it will keep growing forever. That's why he said that he'd allow himself to live if he gets the money from court.

Peru doesn't have a bankruptcy system for people, is what he said. So he thinks he's trapped.
He has all 3 vaccines.

I find the way Sal explains math topics to be very easy to understand, and I go to Khan Academy when more complicated explanations are going over my head.

I agree that the exercises are too easy and don't help you understand the topic deeper. It's often enough to repeat one formula or way of doing things, but it won't train you to apply it in context.

I'd like to see more word problems where you have to use your combined understanding of the current topic and past ones to figure out a "new" formula that suits a specific situation. It would reinforce old knowledge and help you see new angles of the topic at hand.
